# kubectl gentian synopsis

The synopsis of every `kubectl gentian` command, as the plugin's own header states it; the full description of each command is in [commands.md](commands.md).

## 1. Synopsis

```text
  kubectl gentian login                       sign in (a code to confirm in a browser)
  kubectl gentian logout
  kubectl gentian whoami

  kubectl gentian tenants list
  kubectl gentian tenants show <name>
  kubectl gentian tenants create <name> [--display-name <text>] [--no-mfa] [--admins-add-catalogues]
                                 [--self-sign-up]
                                 [--country <ISO 3166-1 alpha-2, e.g. CH>]
                                 (sign-up is off, and is said out loud when it is on:
                                 anybody may make an account)
  kubectl gentian tenants set <name> [--admins-add-catalogues=true|false]
                                     [--country <alpha-2> | --country ""]   "" names none
  kubectl gentian tenants activate-admin <name> [--recovery-email <address>]
  kubectl gentian tenants retire <name> [--purge [--keep-bundles]] [--yes]
  kubectl gentian tenants import <file.gentian> [--identity-file <f> | --passphrase] [--drop-custom-domain]
  kubectl gentian tenants import --bucket <b> --prefix <p> [--endpoint <url> [--addressing-style path|virtualHost]]
                                 (--identity-file <f> | --passphrase) [--drop-custom-domain]
                                 (the bundle's custom domain is kept unless --drop-custom-domain)
  kubectl gentian tenants delegate-catalogues <name> on|off
  kubectl gentian tenants domain <name>                      the domain of its own it is bound to
  kubectl gentian tenants domain <name> <domain> [--yes]     bind it: its addresses move to <label>.<domain>
                                                            (a cluster with many tenants only)
  kubectl gentian tenants domain <name> --remove [--yes]     back to its default address
  kubectl gentian tenants mail-mode <name> [<mode>]          what the operator provisions for its mail:
                                                            selfhosted, external, transport-only, disabled
  kubectl gentian tenants groups <name> [<group>... | --clear]   its own groups, declared in git
  kubectl gentian tenants sign-in <name> [--from <tenant> --groups <g>,... | --remove <tenant>]
                                                            people of another tenant of this cluster signing in here
  kubectl gentian tenants partners <name>                    realms of other clusters its realm links accounts with
  kubectl gentian tenants partners <name> add <partner> --issuer <https://<host>/<path to the realm>>
                                 [--issue] [--accept link|create|organization [--domain <d>] [--display-name <text>]]
                                 [--as <name the partner gives this realm>]
  kubectl gentian tenants partners <name> remove <partner>
  kubectl gentian tenants platform-access <name> [on|off]    whether the platform's administrators may sign in
                                                            to the tenant as its administrators (the tenant's switch)

  kubectl gentian platform-roles holders                     who holds which cluster role by name, as the claim declares
  kubectl gentian platform-roles holders add <role> <tenant> <login> --reason <why> [--expires <RFC 3339>] [--scope tenant:<t>]
                                                            a person of the platform tenant, or an administrator
                                                            of another, holds it: one commit
  kubectl gentian platform-roles holders remove <role> <tenant> <login>   no longer
  kubectl gentian platform-roles candidates                  who could hold one: the platform tenant's people,
                                                            every other tenant's administrators
  kubectl gentian platform-roles members                     who holds admin and breakGlass through their group

  kubectl gentian credentials list [--tenant <tenant>]       what is asked for, and whether it is set
  kubectl gentian credentials set <name> --field <key>=@<file> [--field <key>=-]
                                                            set one; a value from a file, or from stdin (once)

  kubectl gentian catalogues list [--tenant <tenant>]
  kubectl gentian catalogues add <name> <https-url> [--tenant <tenant>]
  kubectl gentian catalogues add <name> --oci <artifact> --repository <repository> [--tenant <tenant>]
                                 a catalog kept as an OCI artifact, read with the credential of a
                                 repository declared for the tenant (or, without --tenant, for the cluster)
  kubectl gentian catalogues remove <name> [--tenant <tenant>]
  kubectl gentian catalogues rename <old> <new> [--tenant <tenant>]
                                 the same catalog under another name: what was installed from
                                 it follows, in the same commit, and no build moves
  kubectl gentian catalogues residue
  kubectl gentian catalogues residue remove <kind>/<name> [--namespace <ns>] [--yes]

  kubectl gentian repositories declare <name> --tenant <tenant> --url oci://<host>/<path> [--type oci]
                                 a private registry a tenant pulls charts and images from;
                                 the token is set in the Admin Console under Credentials
  kubectl gentian repositories remove <name> --tenant <tenant>

  kubectl gentian models list                  the models the gateway offers, and what the claim says of each
  kubectl gentian models show                  the Cluster claim's model settings, as JSON
  kubectl gentian models set -f <file.json>    make the claim declare exactly these settings
                                               (no provider's token: that is a credential)

  kubectl gentian settings show                the Cluster claim's settings, as JSON
  kubectl gentian settings set <path>=<value> [...]   change them, in one commit: tenancyMode=multi,
                                               mainAddress.tenant=<tenant>, mail.serviceMode=system,
                                               platformRoles.auditor=gentian:platform:auditor ...

  kubectl gentian apps list --tenant <tenant> [--available]
  kubectl gentian apps install <app> --tenant <tenant> [--from <source>] [--digest sha256:<hex>] [--for-everyone]
  kubectl gentian apps uninstall <app> --tenant <tenant> [--purge]
  kubectl gentian apps approve <app> --tenant <tenant>       what the app asks for that nobody has approved yet
  kubectl gentian apps approve <app> <kind>/<name> --tenant <tenant> --reason "<why>" [--expires <RFC 3339>]
                                                            approve one request: egress (the tenant's perimeter approver),
                                                            podSecurity or clusterRoles (the cluster's security officer)
  kubectl gentian apps decline <app> <kind>/<name> --tenant <tenant> --reason "<why>"
                                                            decline one, with the same right; the app keeps waiting
  kubectl gentian approvals list                             what awaits the security officer and the perimeter
                                                            approver, across all tenants: who answers, who asked,
                                                            when, why the app wants it, and what was declined
  kubectl gentian approvals granted                          every tenant's approved privilege exceptions

  kubectl gentian exposures requests --tenant <tenant>        what its apps ask to have on the internet, or to keep
                                                              of their own Authorization header behind sign-in
  kubectl gentian exposures approve <app-instance> <entry> --tenant <tenant> [--expires <date>] [--reason <text>]
                                    [--acknowledge-main-address-rule] [--yes]
  kubectl gentian exposures list --tenant <tenant>            what the tenant has on the internet
  kubectl gentian exposures withdraw <app-instance> <entry> --tenant <tenant>
  kubectl gentian exposures alias <app-instance> <entry> --tenant <tenant> (--host <name>.<cluster's domain> | --remove)
                                                              a second address for a published entry, directly under
                                                              the cluster's own domain; the cluster's administrator's

  kubectl gentian resources plans --tenant <tenant>
  kubectl gentian resources show --tenant <tenant>
  kubectl gentian resources set --tenant <tenant> --plan <plan>
  kubectl gentian resources report --tenant <tenant> --from <time> --to <time>

  kubectl gentian version
```
